# image2pdf v1.2.0 — Wavy Security Watermark, Footer Line & EN/ES Layout Parity

A release focused on the watermark: the background texture now flows like real security paper, a readable footer line reinforces the mark, and the page renders the exact same structure in English and Spanish.

## ✨ Added

- **Readable footer watermark line** — the watermark text is also drawn as a single centred line at the bottom of every page: larger (up to 5% of the shorter page edge, auto-shrunk to fit), dark gray at 60% opacity, independent from the background pattern, and only shown when a watermark is set
- **Wavy security texture** — every row of the background pattern follows a sinusoidal baseline (amplitude ≈1.4× the font size, wavelength 0.6× the shorter page edge) drawn as short chords tilted to the curve's tangent: an organic, banknote-style flow instead of a rigid diagonal grid. Verified on the exported PDF: perfect sine (correlation 1.0000), amplitude 20.7 pt, tangent rotation ±20°
- **Smaller pattern text** — 4% → 2.5% of the shorter page edge (≈15 pt on A4), so the texture reads as small legible security text with the footer standing out above it

## 🔧 Fixed

- **Watermark is now truly continuous in the exported PDF** — the stamp grid was anchored to the page's bottom-left corner and laid out in unrotated coordinates while each stamp rotated on its own, leaving the top third of every page (≈33% of the height) and diagonal bands without any watermark. The grid now lives in the rotated frame around the page centre: uniform corner to corner, measured ink coverage ≈53% with **zero empty rows or columns** at 0°, −30° and −45° (was 17–26% with a 273–279 px empty band)
- **No lanes between lines** — row pitch 0.9× → 0.7× the font size plus a golden-ratio phase per row, so neither line gaps nor word-space channels line up vertically (previously 2–3 px white lanes appeared at 0°)
- **Live preview now matches the export** — the preview rendered the watermark text 33% larger than the PDF (stray `×1.33` conversion); it now uses the same pt→px scale
- **English and Spanish render the exact same page skeleton** — the Spanish content shipped as two blocks (the FAQ nested inside the steps card under an `<h3>`, features listed first) while English had three independent cards in the order steps → features → FAQ. Both languages now share the same three-section structure, heading levels and 6 FAQ items; a DOM parity check over the visible element tree reports `STRUCTURE IDENTICAL` (221 nodes in both)
